description:
A live consumer that goes away from the repository also goes away from the packaged tree the next incremental build produces, observed rather than assumed.

## Background

The build output directory persists across builds. A live consumer deleted or renamed in the repository keeps its copy there, and the next build produces a tree that still carries it, unless the run reconciles the subtree it owns. A suite that only ever builds forward never sees this: every assertion passes while the file exists, and the failure appears only after someone removes one.

This is a distinct failure from a stale installed binary, and it has no coverage anywhere in the workspace today. An existing harness already seeds an isolated repository, cold-builds it, mutates the tree, and rebuilds; the mutation this property needs is the removal of a packaged source, and the observation is the produced tree rather than the reported package.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A live consumer removed from the seeded repository is absent from the packaged tree the next incremental rebuild produces, without clearing the build output directory.
- [hard] REQ-02: The assertion runs in an isolated seeded repository, so it never depends on the state of the working checkout.
- [hard] REQ-03: A failure names the file that survived the removal, so the reader sees which reconciliation step did not run.
- [hard] REQ-04: The assertion observes the produced tree, so it holds whether or not the embed has been re-rooted onto it.
title: Pin the assembly's reconciliation of removed sources
